items.note: KEY.1.1 states that one forward invocation adds x_S to y_S for arbitrary scratch values and that three stages swap the banks 'with signs' and restore scratch (lines 728-738). It does not give the map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), the inverse schedule at stage 2, the neighbour rules or the wire counts, and the proof (net change (JV+RG)x) is not reproduced.

KEY.1.2 gives the mechanism: a common frame at a gate commutes with the pointwise gate, so the network's effect is set by the endpoint frames (line 812). The formula D_out S D_in^{-1}, the edge operator D_v D_u^{-1} and the route sign epsilon_w applied to D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} (lines 814-822) are not stated.

The budget sum |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L is derived along the paper's route: telescoping at gates, source sum N and sink sum Wm-N, and Ic decreasing edges each losing h (lines 1066-1071), with L_b/N=100/539. The gate-label table and residual table that establish 'only center 3->4 decreases' are only quoted (KEY.1.3.2), L_c/N and dim F^{x3}=m are missing, and KEY.1.3 wrongly calls neighbouring gate labels orthogonal.

The endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b and the deficit N-2L_b>0, with the N negative source projections each costing one extra rank, are all present (lines 1138-1167). The proof steps 'rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U' and 'P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I' are only implied, the frames Phi_M are not defined, and KEY.1 misdescribes W_b as a number of gates.

R2.1 states that the edge frame changes factor into s_c translation kernels aI+bX_v, that s_c<W_c m and that every role receives C^{tensor m}. It omits the phase frames C_U, the inverse kernels, the count of one kernel per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c and the diagonal corrections, and gives no derivation.

s_b<W_b m (via N-2L_b>0 and L_b/N=100/539), s_c<W_c m and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} (PB.1) are each stated. The relative deficits eta_b, eta_c, the bound eta>20*2^{-50}, log m<20 and the inference s/W<m^tau at that tau (lines 1319-1344) are absent, so the exponent is never tied to the saving.

T.1 and T.2 restate both lemmas faithfully: digit permutations, moves, splits and merges, and cyclic row splitting in O(V); controlled shifts mod q^b and fixed rational units in O(V). T.2's quote carries the b^{O(1)} offset-preparation condition. No derivation is given.

The shear cost follows the paper (lines 1425-1446): lower-triangular transforms in O(V) in descending order, the conjugation order E_2, E_1^{-1}, Pi, E_1, E_2^{-1}, and one interchange per one of Pi. The lower-triangular factorization itself is only quoted (no elimination argument, lines 1375-1391), and the choice of the prime q avoiding all denominators is omitted.

The plan follows the proof: cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} per edge by recursive interchanges, the common-frame identity giving H<-H+D on every row, the three-update interchange, s calls, the recurrence and the geometric sum. The fixed-tape depth-first schedule (lines 1559-1615) that justifies the O(1) normalized node cost is absent, as is the row-divisibility condition W^k.

R1.1-R1.5 follow the proof in order: split off the top rho digits into a row field of range at least W^k, pad rows to a multiple of W^k, cut the rest into base-m pieces, sum O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), and pad binary ranges to [q^e] with e=O(u). Only the unequal-width remark (1740-1762) is not covered.

R2.2 (s_c child calls on f=e/m axes per slot) and R2.3 (H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D) are correct. The conjugation by P_M that places residual directions on coordinate slots, the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z and the fixed number of row additions appear at most as 'binary basis changes' in R2's method.

R2.4.1-R2.4.3 follow the paper: the eight conditional additions flip u's parity and restore w, there are twenty excluded guard values per guard giving delta_bad, and bad records are repaired by extraction and radix sort. The full time bound with its M A^3 and delta_bad terms is reduced to O(V(L^tau+1)) without its conditions. The chunk interchanges that produce the L^tau term, the separate top position j_{f-1}, and the fact that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes only the bad set are not shown.

The row split u=Wg+w with 1/W child volumes and the recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) are stated correctly, and R2.7 asserts the total O(Vd^{lambda'}). The leaf cost F(e)=O(e), the condition s/W<=m^sigma, K<=e^{c/beta}, the q_0-chunk row index and the summation to lambda'>max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)} are missing.

R2's children follow the proof route: phase network, child calls, packed basis changes, row streams, the recurrence, total time, guard widths o(p) and one final truncation, and conversion to H_0 by S_D. The statement omits K=floor(d^c), the error bound sqrt2 2^{-p} and the parameter conditions. The derivation lacks the P_M conjugation, the row preprocessing and the unrolling conditions.

The plan gives the roots y^{2r/t}, character cancellation with F^+F^-=t^{-1}I, the bit-reversed outputs B_tF_t^- and F_t^+B_t^{-1}, and rounds grouped as one butterfly plus a monomial shift. It also gives the layout by O(dK) prefix moves and at most Dq-1 width-K exchanges costing O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), one simultaneous layer per round, error sqrt2 ell 2^{-p}, and the exact operators LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, all matching lines 2990-3189.

The derivation matches: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, four products with the established multiplier on absolute values, |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2 for centred residues, the negacyclic fold and O(rp log(rp)). The lemma's output Q_p(fg/r) with error below sqrt2 2^{-p} is not stated; the plan claims only the exact product.

The plan states M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T with error sqrt2 M(3ell+1)2^{-p} and the stated cost. It derives the result by two forward transforms kept in LB order, packed products, the opposite transform with scaling by M, the normalization check and P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), as at lines 3414-3473.

The identities P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA and RF_s=2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A with gamma=2d alpha^2 are correct, as is the line-map cost. P_s and P_t are never defined, the approximations' error and the axis-exposure cost are missing, and G.1.2 cites A=S', B_0=D'J'C without the Gaussian maps S, T, the selection C or the left-inverse argument (lines 3576-3640).

The plan gives the chirp identity with its period and coefficient check, and the cancellation via F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+, RF^+R=F^+, a permutation commuting with pointwise products, and the two normalizations giving (u*v)/S^2. This matches the proof at 3938-3983.

The exponents (missing lambda, delta, beta), sizes b, p, d, K, T, r and the prime interval are stated. The prime existence, distinctness, T/2<S<T, the resampling hypotheses and the n^{o(1)} search follow the paper. eta=1/(4d) and alpha are never given, and the size estimates eq:sizes are not derived.

The plan gives Phi as an isomorphism because x maps to an element of order S, the triangular update b_i as a prefix-controlled cyclic shift, and O(d^2) unequal-width axis swaps for O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)), as in the paper.

The plan gives that the map is well defined via (zeta y)^r=1, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=f*g/T, and the computed truncated twists. The error 6TL 2^{-p} matches line 4617.

The source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, scale 2^gamma; exact counterpart RF_s; opposite by conjugation) and the six algorithm steps are given, including the two scalings by S and 2^{2b+4}S that undo (u*v)/S^2. The input digit scaling 2^{-b-2} is not mentioned.

The final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, the product error (2E_s+2)2^{-p}, the 2^{2b+4}S scaling and the carries are correct. The error chain that defines the inputs (E_ring<5TL, chirp <8TL, E_s=9 2^gamma TL, E_w=S(3E_s+2)) and the use of gamma<=b/4 are not shown.

The plan gives the final steps: seven margins with minimum 2^{-181}=2kappa, log factors absorbed into p^kappa, O(Tp p^{1-kappa}), and schoolbook below a cutoff. It never lists the seven normalized cost rows or the margins g_1..g_7, and omits the o(V) setup and exceptional sorting.
ROOT relies on 'nlogn-conjecture', and its motivation contrasts the bound with n log n. No step states that one machine with liminf T(n)/(n lg n)=0 refutes the eventual lower bound.

errors.says: Labels built from triple indicator vectors are nested along every edge 'and the labels of neighboring gates are orthogonal'.
errors.paper: What is orthogonal are neighbouring triple lines t_S, t_T (lines 869-870, 953). Gate labels are not orthogonal; every edge joins comparable (nested) labels (lines 998, 1061).

errors.says: 'A fixed network of W_b pointwise XOR gates'.
errors.paper: W_b is the number of wires; the network has W_b wires and uses only pointwise XOR gates (lines 778-779, 1139).

errors.says: Motivation: 'm^k=e levels' growth is read off the geometric sum'.
errors.paper: The recursion has k levels, with e=m^k; the geometric sum sum_{j=0}^k a^j is over k+1 terms (lines 1554-1557).

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. The KEY branch (fixed bank-exchange network, frames, labels, rank budget, endpoint identity, matrix shear, recurrence) feeds R1 and, through R2's complex network, R2/R3/R4. R3/R4 then feed G and PB, ending with the margin computation. It thins out at the exponent, where tau=1-2^{-50} appears only in PB.1 and is never tied to s/W<m^tau through eta and log m<20. It also thins out on the complex side, where the phase interface, the P_M conjugation and the layer recurrence's unrolling are quoted rather than derived, and in the error chain, cost rows and fixed-tape schedule, which are asserted without their content.

steps.note: The fixed scalar network is there with its mechanism: an eight-row copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule adding x_S to y_S for arbitrary scratch, and three stages that swap the banks with signs and restore every scratch wire, on data indexed by three-element subsets tensored three times. The numerical data h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3, and the explicit (-Y_a,X_a), are absent; it counts as reconstructed only on the mechanism.

KEY.1.2 states that a common invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, so the overall effect is set by the endpoint frames. KEY.1's motivation makes each edge a change of frame. The explicit operator D_out S D_in^{-1} is not written.

Labels are tensor-cubed triple-indicator subspaces. Neighbouring triple lines are nondegenerate and orthogonal, every edge joins comparable labels, and the only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h. dim F^{x3}=m is not stated, and KEY.1.3 misworded orthogonality as being between gate labels.

Projections are taken as frames, an edge is cheap when its nested labels differ in few dimensions, the dimension sum is turned into the rank sum, and the N negative source projections each cost one extra rank. The identity rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U is only implied by 'so', not stated; this is a borderline credit.
The plan gives sum |Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L by telescoping, source sum N and sink sum Wm-N, and Ic decreasing edges of loss h (so L=Ich). It also gives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
The plan gives L_b/N=100/539<1/2 and the deficit N-2L_b>0, so s_b<W_b m. The complex ratio 101/539 is not given, but the bit chain is complete.

The plan states M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m for every input role and that, after merging, the common-frame identity leaves H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included. Why the difference is I_m (sources -P_{U_a}, sinks P_{U_a^perp}) is not given.
The plan gives the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2, a lower-triangular O(V) step, the conjugation order, one interchange per one of Pi so exactly a interchanges plus O(V), and s recursive calls at a node.

Children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau and F_k=O(e^tau) are all present, and tau=1-2^{-50} appears in PB.1. The justification of that tau (eta>20*2^{-50}, log m<20) is absent, so the explicit exponent is unlinked; the credit rests on the recurrence.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the central chain essentially completely on the bit side, in the order the paper uses: fixed network, frames, labels, ranks as dimension changes with the N source exceptions, the budget, L_b/N=100/539 giving s<Wm, the endpoint identity, edges as rank-many recursive calls, and the recurrence. The weak points are the network's numerical data (h, N, m), the implicit projection-rank identity, and the missing derivation of tau=1-2^{-50} from the deficit.
